method: WebSearch + WebFetch; every URL below was opened during this run
notes: Anthropic's own docs are used as a primary source for concrete numbers, and are labelled as vendor documentation rather than neutral fact. Cross-vendor comparison pages carry the comparison claims.

The tokenizer-change note on the Anthropic pricing page is unusually valuable: it is a vendor stating on the record that the same text produces ~30% more tokens after a tokenizer change. It makes the 'a token is not a stable unit' point concrete without hand-waving.

w1.m01.b01.title: Tool use overview
w1.m01.b01.claim: A model emits a structured tool-call request; the surrounding program executes it and returns a result into context.

w1.m01.b01.title: Pricing
w1.m01.b01.claim: Declaring tools adds a measurable, documented number of input tokens to every request (286-675 depending on model).
w1.m01.b01.notes: Concrete evidence that the harness has a token cost, not just a conceptual one.

w1.m01.b02.title: Attention Is All You Need
w1.m01.b02.claim: The Transformer dispenses with recurrence and convolution, relying entirely on attention to relate positions in a sequence.

w1.m01.b02.title: Parity-Aware Byte-Pair Encoding: Improving Cross-lingual Fairness in Tokenization
w1.m01.b02.claim: Per-language token cost is unequal under classical BPE; the paper reduces the Gini coefficient of per-language cost by up to 89%.
w1.m01.b02.notes: Submitted 2025-08-06, last revised 2026-07-02. Establishes that billing per token transfers tokenizer bias onto users as unequal cost and latency.

w1.m01.b02.title: Pricing — tokenizer note
w1.m01.b02.claim: Claude 4.7 and later use a newer tokenizer that produces approximately 30% more tokens for the same text than earlier models.
w1.m01.b02.notes: A vendor on the record that token counts are not comparable across model generations.

w1.m01.b03.title: Why Language Models Hallucinate
w1.m01.b03.publisher: Kalai, Nachum, Vempala, Zhang — OpenAI and Georgia Tech, arXiv
w1.m01.b03.claim: Hallucination is a predictable statistical consequence of training and evaluation that reward guessing over abstention; binary scoring makes a guess strictly better than 'I don't know'.

w1.m01.b03.title: Evaluating large language models for accuracy incentivizes hallucinations
w1.m01.b03.claim: Accuracy-only evaluation creates an incentive structure that produces confident false answers.
w1.m01.b03.notes: Peer-reviewed treatment of the same result; cite alongside the arXiv preprint.

w1.m01.b03.title: Context windows
w1.m01.b03.claim: Everything in a request counts toward the window — system prompt, messages, tool results, images, tool definitions, and generated output including thinking. Accuracy and recall degrade as the window fills ('context rot'). Input over the limit returns a 400; generation that reaches it stops with model_context_window_exceeded.

w1.m01.b04.title: Pricing
w1.m01.b04.claim: Per-model input/output rates, cache read at 0.1x base input, cache write at 1.25x (5m) or 2x (1h), Batch API at 50% off, 1M context at standard pricing on 4.6+.

w1.m01.b04.title: LLM API pricing comparison in 2026
w1.m01.b04.claim: Cross-vendor flagship rates as of 2026: GPT-5.6 Sol $5/$30 at 1.05M context; Claude Opus 5 $5/$25 at 1M; Gemini 3.1 Pro $2/$12 at 1M with a higher tier above 200K input.
w1.m01.b04.notes: Aggregator. Cross-checked against Anthropic's own page for the Claude column; treat the other columns as indicative and re-verify before quoting.

w1.m01.b04.title: LLM Context Window Comparison (2026)
w1.m01.b04.claim: Context windows across ~20 models range from 200K to 10M as of 2026.

w1.m01.b05.title: Tool use overview
w1.m01.b05.claim: Tool definitions, tool_use blocks and tool_result blocks are all ordinary context; parallel tool calls return in a single user message.

w1.m01.b05.title: Pricing — tool use pricing
w1.m01.b05.claim: Server-side tools carry usage pricing beyond tokens: web search $10 per 1,000 searches; web fetch no additional cost; code execution 1,550 free container-hours per org per month then $0.05/hour.

w1.m01.b06.title: Attention Is All You Need
w1.m01.b06.claim: Attention computes a weighted combination over all positions, which is the mechanism behind association-driven behaviour.

w1.m01.b06.title: Context windows — context rot
w1.m01.b06.claim: More context is not automatically better; accuracy and recall degrade as token count grows, so curating context matters as much as capacity.
